Figure 6 illustrates a comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations in a model, presenting data from six separate plots arranged in a 3x2 grid. The horizontal axis (x-axis) in all plots is labeled "Layer" and uses a linear scale, with values ranging from 0 to 20, marked at intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20). The vertical axis (y-axis) varies between plots: the left column plots, titled "Massive Activation of..." and "Max Activation Value," use a linear scale with a range from 0 to 1600, marked at intervals of 200. The right column plots, titled "first token attention score of..." and "first token attention score," use a linear scale with a range from 0.0 to 1.0, marked at intervals of 0.2. All plots contain a horizontal dashed line representing the mean value of the "first token attention score," with the specific mean value labeled in each plot.

In the top-left plot ("Massive Activation of baseline"), three lines are shown: a red line for "attn_output" that starts near 0 and rises to a peak of approximately 1600 at layer 15 before decreasing; a green line for "attn_residual" that remains near 0 across all layers; and a blue line for "ffn_output" that remains near 0. The top-right plot ("first token attention score of baseline") shows a blue line for "first token attention score" that fluctuates between approximately 0.4 and 1.0, with a mean of 0.467 indicated by a dashed green line. In the middle-left plot ("Massive Activation of v elementwise"), a red line for "attn_output" rises from 0 to approximately 400 at layer 20, while the green "attn_residual" and blue "ffn_output" lines remain near 0. The middle-right plot ("first token attention score of v elementwise") shows a blue line for "first token attention score" fluctuating between 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.299 indicated by a dashed green line. In the bottom-left plot ("Massive Activation of atten output gate, head share"), the red "attn_output" line rises from 0 to a peak of approximately 1600 at layer 15, the green "attn_residual" line remains near 0, and the blue "ffn_output" line remains near 0. The bottom-right plot ("first token attention score of atten output gate, head share") shows a blue line for "first token attention score" fluctuating between approximately 0.2 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.301 indicated by a dashed green line. In the bottom-left plot ("Massive Activation of atten output gate, w/o sparsity"), the red "attn_output" line rises from 0 to a peak of approximately 1600 at layer 15, the green "attn_residual" line remains near 0, and the blue "ffn_output" line remains near 0. The bottom-right plot ("first token attention score of atten output gate, w/o sparsity") shows a blue line for "first token attention score" fluctuating between approximately 0.4 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.481 indicated by a dashed green line.
model_annotations.Chinese: Figure 6 presents a comparative analysis of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations in a neural network model. The figure is organized into four rows, each comparing a different gating method. The left column of each row displays a plot of "Massive Activation Value" against "Layer," with the y-axis ranging from 0 to 1600 (in increments of 200) and the x-axis representing the layer number from 0 to 25. The right column of each row shows a plot of "First token attention score" against "Layer," with the y-axis ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 (in increments of 0.2) and the x-axis also spanning from 0 to 25. In all plots, the red line, representing "attn_output," shows a significant increase in activation or attention score, peaking around layer 6 in the first row and later in the subsequent rows, with a value of approximately 1400 in the first row and 1200 in the fourth row. The green line, "fm_residual," remains relatively low and stable across all layers, with values close to 0. The blue line, "attn_residual," exhibits a more complex pattern, with a moderate increase in activation or attention score, peaking around layer 6 in the first two rows and later in the third and fourth rows, with a value of approximately 1000 in the first row and 800 in the fourth row. The dashed green line, "fm_output," remains low and stable, with values close to 0. The plots in the right column also show that the "first token attention score" for "attn_output" peaks around layer 6 in the first two rows and later in the third and fourth rows, with a value of approximately 1.0 in the first row and 0.8 in the fourth row. The "attn_residual" line shows a more complex pattern, with a moderate increase in attention score, peaking around layer 6 in the first two rows and later in the third and fourth rows, with a value of approximately 0.6 in the first row and 0.4 in the fourth row. The "fm_output" line remains low and stable, with values close to 0. The mean attention score for "attn_output" is 0.467 in the first row, 0.468 in the second row, 0.297 in the third row, and 0.465 in the fourth row. The mean attention score for "attn_residual" is 0.301 in the third row and 0.301 in the fourth row.
model_annotations.English: Figure 6 presents a comparative analysis of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations in a neural network model. The figure is structured as a 4x2 grid of line plots, with the left column showing the "Massive Activation" and the right column showing the "first token attention score" for various configurations. The x-axis, labeled "Layer," spans from 0 to 25 and is linearly scaled, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis on the left plots "Massive Activation Value" with a scale ranging from 0 to 1600, while the y-axis on the right plots "first token attention score" on a scale from 0.0 to 1.0. Each plot contains multiple lines representing different components of the model, such as "attn_output," "fm_output," and "fm_residual," with distinct colors and line styles. For instance, in the top-left plot, the "attn_output" line (red, solid) shows a significant increase, peaking around layer 10 with a value of approximately 1400, while the "fm_output" line (green, dashed) remains low. The "first token attention score" plots on the right show more fluctuation, with the "first token attention score" line (blue, solid) exhibiting peaks and troughs, and a horizontal green dashed line indicating the mean score. The caption below the figure explains that Row 1 (Baseline) shows significant activations and attention sinks after the 6th layer, Row 2 (SDPA Gating) shows reduced activations and no attention sinks, and Rows 3-5 (Value Layer Gating) show similar activations to Row 2 but with residual attention sinks, while Rows 4-5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid) show massive activations and attention sinks that resemble the baseline.
